title: Data-quality audit
result: 43.2% of urban BioSamples lack a resolved place; 106,803 have a place and a plausible full date. 180 samples have impossible collection dates and are excluded from temporal tests.

title: Global blind spots of urban genomic surveillance
result: Concentration index 0.82 (95% CI 0.62–0.91); 224 of 573 cities of ≥1 M people have no urban sample within 50 km.

title: Surveillance capacity and economic development
result: A 1% higher GDP per capita goes with 1.27% more urban samples per person (95% CI 0.86–1.69, p=1.7e-09), across 159 countries.

title: COVID-19 and the structure of urban sequencing
result: Level change at 2020-03: 30% (p=0.46); trend change -2%/yr (p=0.87). Wastewater share 67% → 84%.

title: Habitat representation
result: Habitat evenness 0.51; municipal wastewater holds 71% of urban samples. Least-studied: transit, surfaces_infrastructure, built_environment. Habitat mix differs by continent (χ²=277, p=6.1e-39).

title: Metadata completeness
result: Joint Wald tests of the assay terms: has_place (p=5.6e-07), has_coordinates (p=1.8e-10), has_collection_date (p=2.1e-08), has_env_broad_scale (p=3.3e-08)

title: Concentration in few centres
result: The top 1% of 1,491 submitting centres (15) hold 43% of urban samples; the top 10 hold 38%.

title: Diffusion of sequencing technologies
result: long_read: 48/66 countries adopted, median lag 3 y; illumina_novaseq: 55/66 countries adopted, median lag 4 y; dnbseq_bgi: 13/66 countries adopted, median lag 0 y

title: Eligibility-screen benchmark
result: Labeling sheet of 500 BioSamples written. Label them (two raters, blind to the tier in labeling_key.tsv) and rerun with --labels.
